title: [YouPass Collect] - The proportion of 14- to 16-year-old students studying a foreign language in an English speaking country, and the top three foreign languages
prompt: The two bar charts below show the proportion of 14- to 16-year-old students studying a foreign language in an English speaking country, and the top three foreign languages. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The given bar charts compare the percentages of male and female students, aged from 14 to 16 years old, learning another language, and the three most common languages studied in an English-speaking country.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, females engaged in learning a foreign language in greater numbers than their male counterparts, and both genders' interests in this activity decreased over the given period. In addition, though French remained the most chosen language, both French and German declined in popularity, while the opposite was true for Spanish.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at participation rates, in 1984, nearly half of female students studied a foreign language, compared to 30% of males. After 23 years, both genders witnessed a decrease in interest in this activity, with the figures for females and males dropping to 40% and 25%, respectively.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the three languages shown, in 1984, French was the most popular, with half of all the students studying this language. In a distant second place was German, at 20%, and Spanish came third, with a negligible 5%. Thereafter, the percentage of students opting for French halved, ending up at 25% in the later year. Similarly, German became less preferred, as it was studied by only 15% of students by the end of the period. In contrast, the percentage of Spanish learners doubled, reaching 10% by 2007.
